Smooth echo and DRAG leakage sweep

Three-level AC-Stark-corrected spectroscopy across pulse length and Lorentzian cutoff.

L = 3, 5, 7, 10, 20, 30 us cutoff c = 0.001, 0.005, 0.02 Rabi = 10-80 MHz alpha/2pi = -216 MHzT1/T2 = 51.24/7.31 us
18+1grid settings plus focused comparison
4protocols per shape
≤1 nsRK4 time step

Pulse construction

The current echo uses an instantaneous sign reversal. The smooth versions replace it by a peak-normalized -tanh(t/tau) zero crossing with tau=2 ns. DRAG uses Omega_Q=-beta d(Omega_I)/dt/alpha with beta=1 and the derivative of the complete signed waveform.

AC-Stark phase and kappa

delta f_corr(t) = kappa [Omega_I(t)/(2 pi)]^2; phi(t) = 2 pi integral delta f_corr(t) dt

The first three protocols retain the reference kappa=+0.00225 MHz^-1. The fourth protocol retunes kappa independently for every duration/cutoff pair by minimizing the RMS fitted center over the complete 10-80 MHz grid.

The center tracker follows the local minimum nearest zero inside +/-120 kHz. Large residuals at weak contrast mean that one amplitude-independent kappa no longer describes the line reliably; they should not be interpreted as precise frequency shifts.

FFT convention

The spectra use the complete complex played envelope at Omega0/(2 pi)=80 MHz, including the accumulated kappa phase and, where applicable, the DRAG quadrature. Each pulse-length panel uses one shared amplitude normalization for all four protocols. Dotted lines mark +/-|alpha|/(2 pi)=216 MHz. No analysis window is applied, so the finite pulse truncation remains visible; zero padding only samples the FFT more densely. The -100 dB floor is for display.

Individual-map display

The map explorer contains all 72 duration/cutoff/protocol scans. P_e uses the fixed 0-1 population scale; P_f uses one shared logarithmic scale with a 1e-06 display floor. The embedded maps are 16-bit display encodings, while the NPZ files retain full precision.

Interpretation boundary

This is a three-level rotating-wave simulation. The reported leakage is final P_f, not maximum transient leakage. No measured microwave transfer function or predistortion is included, and the fitted coefficients are not hardware calibrations. The FFT is a waveform diagnostic, not the nonlinear qutrit response itself.

Literature basis: Motzoi et al. (2009), Gambetta et al. (2011), and Hyyppa et al. (2024).
